builder_plan.scenario: An assistant chooses the wrong API or sends arguments your product cannot use.
builder_plan.change: Apply the proposed tool-selection or argument-generation change in a sandbox.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current agent with the same tool schemas and task budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct completed actions, invalid calls, retries, latency, and cost per completed task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: SkillBrowser: Selective Skill Exposure for Scalable Skill-Using Agents
summary: SkillBrowser replaces static retrieval of skills from the initial task query, and one-shot LLM-based catalog selection, with a Meta-Skill that identifies emerging capability needs during reasoning, issues targeted queries, and loads skills on demand. It costs an additional orchestration layer plus extra LLM calls, which the paper acknowledges as added latency and added inference expense per task. It can fail through under-invocation of useful skills, and its benefits are model- and task-dependent, so weaker base models may not formulate effective skill queries.
rationale: The approach is implementable with API-based LLMs and requires no training, but the paper itself reports model- and task-dependent gains, under-invocation failures, and latency overhead, so adoption should follow a workload-specific A/B evaluation against the reader's current retrieval baseline.

claims.statement: SkillBrowser replaces static retrieval of skills from the initial task query, and one-shot LLM-based catalog selection, with a Meta-Skill that identifies emerging capability needs during reasoning, issues targeted queries, and loads skills on demand. It costs an additional orchestration layer plus extra LLM calls, which the paper acknowledges as added latency and added inference expense per task. It can fail through under-invocation of useful skills, and its benefits are model- and task-dependent, so weaker base models may not formulate effective skill queries.

Improves aggregate accuracy over static retrieval and LLM-based skill selection across six SRA-Bench subsets and five LLMs, including multi-step tool use, while reducing accuracy degradation on already-solvable instances; no factor is reported in the abstract.
